result.text:
Your kid wants a drone.

DJI Mini 4K: $299. It films in 4K. It weighs under 249 grams. It comes with a remote.

Flix is the other kind. An ESP32, four motors, a 3D-printed frame. 2.1k stars. The flight code is under 2,000 lines. Short enough to read in an afternoon.

The sensor reads the tilt. The code levels the motors. You steer.

A phone can fly it over Wi-Fi. So can a USB gamepad. So can a normal remote. No app store account.

Gazebo runs the same Arduino code on screen before you arm the real one. Break the plastic, print another. The frame files are STL and STEP, in the repo.

There is a Python library for scripted flights. A wireless command line. A flight-control textbook, still being written. Position hold is on the list. It is not done.

One honest note. This is not a DJI. No camera. No GPS. A crash can break more than the frame. The author says it may not fly, and is not responsible for injury.

If you want the video, buy the Mini 4K. If you want to read how a drone stays in the air, build a Flix.

(Link in the comments)

meet ESP32-C3 AdBlock, an open-source DIY DNS ad blocker by ZedAxis, built around a roughly $2 ESP32-C3 Super Mini board

inside: 400 KB of RAM, 4 MB of flash, built-in Wi-Fi and a USB adapter, tucked into a printed case

no subscription

no browser extension

no separate power brick

plug it into your router’s USB port for power, connect over Wi-Fi and set it as your DNS server to block listed ad and tracker domains.

compact 40-bit hashes save RAM. a web dashboard lets you check blocked requests and add domains, 

while open-source code and case files let you build your own.
